description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while restoring perl-tests/loopctl.t's
inline `ok(1,'SKIP')` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING.  Two failure modes, one
cause.

REPRO A -- silent (scratch/p27-dyn-last-loops.pl):

    sub do_last { last }
    my $n = 0;
    for my $i (1..3) { $n++; do_last(); $n += 100; }
    print "n=$n\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  n=1     (the loop is exited on the first iteration)
  PCL:          n=303   (the `last` does NOTHING; all three iterations run
                         and the statement after the call runs each time)

REPRO B -- a crash (scratch/p28-dyn-next-crash.pl):

    sub do_next { next }
    my $n = 0; my $g = 0;
    while ($g++ < 3) { $n++; do_next(); $n += 100; }

  perl 5.40.3:  n=3
  PCL:          Unhandled sb-int:compiled-program-error --
                  Form: (go :next)
                  Compile-time error: attempt to GO to nonexistent tag: :next

THE MECHANISM IS IN THE ERROR: PCL lowers a bare `next`/`last` to a LEXICAL CL
`(go :next)` / `(go :last)`.  A CL `go` tag is lexically scoped, so inside a
sub compiled on its own there is no such tag; SBCL compiles the form with an
error and only signals when it is reached.  The `for` spelling reaches a
different lowering that swallows it instead, which is the worse half -- a
silent wrong of the #964 kind.

THE LABELLED FORM IS ALREADY RIGHT (probed, scratch/p26-dyn-last.pl):
`sub f { last OUTER } OUTER: { f(); $ok = 0 }` gives ok=1 in both, so a
non-local exit mechanism EXISTS -- the bare form just does not use it.  That
is the likely fix shape: lower an unlabelled `last`/`next`/`redo` the way the
labelled one is lowered, against the INNERMOST dynamically-enclosing loop
frame rather than a lexical tag.  perl's own model is dynamic (it warns
"Exiting subroutine via last" precisely because it is crossing a frame), so
matching it is not an extension.

RULE-12 NOTE: even before the fix, REPRO A must not be silent.  A `(go :tag)`
the compiler knows cannot resolve should announce, not be emitted and left to
SBCL -- and the `for` path should not swallow the exit at all.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/loopctl.t row 41 `dynamically scoped`
(`sub test_last { last }` called from inside a bare block; PCL falls through
and sets $ok = 0).  Row 40 `dynamically scoped label`, the labelled twin,
passes.  Restored in s464ay and DELIBERATELY NOT registered as a skip -- it is
a fix target, in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv with this task as its cause.  The
same rows are in the companion t/op/loopctl.t inside its blessed count.

THE WRONG DIAGNOSIS IT HID BEHIND: the inline skip said "dynamically scoped
last across function boundary not supported in PCL" -- true as far as it goes,
but written as a feature absence, so nobody measured that the ordinary
`for`-loop spelling silently mis-executes and the `while` spelling crashes.
Its neighbour in the same file blamed "foreach loop var aliasing not supported
in PCL", which is FLATLY FALSE (probed: bug 37725 passes), so the file's
comments cannot be trusted as a cause index.
=== HALF (a) SHIPPED (s470bi); HALF (b) NOT WRITTEN â with the numbers ===
HALF (a), per the Fable ruling of s470.  A bare `last`/`next`/`redo` whose
nearest enclosing loop is not inside the sub body now DIES at run time, at its
own site, trappably:
  PCL: unsupported: "last" exiting subroutine NAME (dynamic loop exit; docs/not-supported.md)
and a bare exit with NO loop anywhere keeps perl's own text,
`Can't "last" outside a loop block`.  Repro A is no longer silent (it printed
n=303 where perl says 1) and repro B no longer reaches SBCL's "attempt to GO to
nonexistent tag".  ONE document walk (`_mark_dynamic_loop_exits`) and ONE
emission site; the verdict rides the TOKEN through `@PPI_ADHOC_KEYS`, because
the keyword reaches the emitter by several parse paths.

WHAT COUNTS AS AN ENCLOSING LOOP -- every answer probed, and the two
non-obvious ones were caught by the emission A/B rather than by a probe:
  * PPI compound types `for` (C-style), `foreach`, `while` (= `until`),
    `continue` (a BARE BLOCK is ALWAYS this type -- labelled or not, first
    statement or not), plus `label`.  **Missing `for` would have killed
    perl-tests/my.t and time.t**, which both put a `last` in a C-style for.
  * **a `for`/`foreach` STATEMENT MODIFIER is a loop, with no Compound around
    it** -- core Exporter.pm's `import` is written
    `($heavy = /\W/) and last foreach (@_);` precisely to avoid entering a
    block scope, so marking it would have made every `use` die.
  * a `while`/`until` MODIFIER is NOT a loop -- measured, not symmetry: perl
    answers `Can't "last" outside a loop block` for
    `$i++ and last while $i < 5`, the same rule that makes `do BLOCK while (â¦)`
    not a loop.
  * the walk's arm ORDER is load-bearing: `PPI::Statement::Sub` and
    `::Compound` are both `PPI::Statement`.
  * a LABELLED exit is never marked -- it already lowers correctly.

MEASURED COST OF (a), and it is why (b) matters.  Across the whole perl-tests
corpus the mark fires at exactly ONE site -- `sub test_last { last }` in
perl-tests/loopctl.t, the row this task owns -- and the call is not inside an
eval, so the file aborts there:
    perl-tests/loopctl.t   OK 63/1  ->  PARTIAL 40/0     (-23 passing rows)
    t/op/loopctl.t         -23 passing rows
    t/op/rt119311.t        -3      (six `{ foo(sub { â¦; last }) }` sites,
                                    testing a DESTROY-during-unwind bug)
That is the s329 archetype's own cost shape, incurred knowingly under the
ruling.  **The baselines were deliberately NOT edited** -- 26 blessed rows is
Fable's call -- and half (a) is a SEPARATE commit so it can be held or
reverted on its own.

HALF (b) â NOT WRITTEN, and the design is the ruling's, unchanged:
catch-ONCE-per-loop-ENTRY, never per iteration:
    (loop (catch 'p-loop-dyn (return (progn <the whole loop>))) <step/advance>)
with the loop state living OUTSIDE the catch, so a caught `next` throw does the
step and re-enters, a caught `last` returns, and `redo` re-enters without the
step; the throw VALUE says which.  Emit the catch frame only for loops whose
body contains a CALL (a loop with no call cannot be exited dynamically), and
measure whether even that is free on `tools/bench-exec.pl`'s counting rows
(print the control spread beside every number; re-measure any mover three
times).  A throw with no catch = the (a) die.

WHY IT WAS NOT ATTEMPTED IN s470bi: it needs a rework of every loop macro in
the runtime (the state must live outside the catch so re-entry resumes) plus a
compiler-side "body contains a call" gate, and the ruling requires a bench
measurement on a quiet box.  The brief's own fallback applies -- "(a) alone
ships and (b) goes in the task with the numbers" -- and the numbers above are
an argument FOR doing (b) next rather than against it.

GUARD `Pl/t/loop-exit-01.t` (8 rows, 1 s): the two failure modes, the
trappability, perl's own text for the no-loop case, and inverse rows covering
foreach / C-style for / labelled-exit-from-a-sub / bare block / `while` inside
the sub / a plain `next` in its own loop.  Inverse-verified against main: rows
1-5 fail there, rows 6-8 pass on both.  `docs/not-supported.md` carries the
entry, including what must NOT be marked and why.

=== HALF (b) BUILT AND MEASURED (s470bl) â NOT MERGED, ONE BLOCKER (#1162) ===
The design is the s470 Fable one, unchanged, and it WORKS: 53 probes vs perl
5.40.3 all match (every loop shape x last/next/redo, two-level chains,
innermost-wins, a map block, a string eval, a coderef through a sub, the
foreach element identity under redo).  Both original repros are answered:
`sub do_last { last }` in a foreach gives n=1 (was 303) and
`sub do_next { next }` in a while gives n=3 g=4 (was "GO to nonexistent tag").

MECHANISM.  Exit site -> `(%p-dyn-loop-exit :last)`: throw the keyword to the
shared tag `p-loop-dyn` when a frame is active (catch picks the innermost,
which IS perl's rule), else die with perl's own `Can't "last" outside a loop
block`, trappably.  Loop -> `:dyn t` licenses ONE catch + ONE special bind per
loop ENTRY; the loop's STATE is outside the catch and a caught throw re-enters
the iteration tagbody where the LEXICAL exit would have arrived.
`%p-loop-driver` is the one implementation for p-while / p-for / both foreach
expanders; a bare block gets the wrapper `p-dyn-once` (a loop-once has no
state, so `redo` is a restart).  Kind-A gate `dyn-loop-exit`; with it OFF the
frame-less loops AND half (a)'s die come back together.

NUMBERS (all on the s470bl branch, `e8bfc83`):
  * perl-tests/loopctl.t   PARTIAL 40/0/67 -> OK 64/0/67, FULLY PASSING â
    one row BETTER than the pre-(a) 63/1, because test 41 `dynamically
    scoped` used to fail and now passes.
  * t/op/rt119311.t        8/2 -> 11/2 (its pre-(a) value).
  * t/op/loopctl.t         40/0 -> 0/0   <-- THE BLOCKER, task #1162:
    SBCL's COMPILE heap, measured to the form and discriminated by replacing
    `catch` with `progn`.  NOT blessed â a file at 0 rows is a regression.
  * bench A/B (gate on vs off, same tree, 3 rounds, BENCH_K=3): every row
    0.96-1.02x, inside its own run-to-run spread; 21 of the 27 bench rows are
    emitted BYTE-IDENTICALLY either way.
  * emission vs d54b798, token by token over the corpus: gate off 49 files
    differ (only `(block nil` â the #1160 fix), gate on 97 differ (only the
    frames and the throw sites), 0 UNEXPLAINED both ways.
    emission-ab over 1035 files: RCDIFF 0.
  * gate 203 files / 6927 tests; guard Pl/t/loop-exit-01.t 22 rows.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK, all LOUD and all filed: a `continue` block on a foreach or
a bare block declines the frame (#1161); a `last` inside an overload/tie/
DESTROY handler is refused by PERL TOO, and PCL diverges only when an OUTER
loop holds a frame (#1163); a `sort` comparator is a boundary in perl and is
not one in PCL (#1164).  A LABELLED dynamic exit was never a residue â half
(a) never marked those and they work on both sides (probed).

WHAT NOT TO RETRY: the frame's SHAPE is not the compile-heap problem (the
NLX-free rewrite conses MORE); neither is the nesting; neither is
`notinline`/`compilation-speed`/`speed 0`.  #1162 has the numbers and the one
fix that would work.

=== HALF (b) SHIPPED (s470bl), WITH THE #1162 LICENCE â #1022 CLOSED ===
The compile-heap blocker recorded above was ruled by Fable in the same session
(#1162, now completed): the licence is REACHABILITY BY NAME, not "the body
calls user code".  With it, `t/op/loopctl.t` carries ONE frame instead of 88
and produces 67 rows at the default heap; the whole `perl-tests` corpus carries
one frame; ALL 27 bench rows are emitted byte-identically with the gate on or
off, so the bench cannot move.

FINAL NUMBERS: perl-tests/loopctl.t 40/0 -> 64/0 FULLY PASSING (one better than
the pre-(a) 63/1); t/op/loopctl.t 40/0 -> 64/3 (pre-(a) 63/4); t/op/rt119311.t
8/2 -> 11/2.  All five baselines edited ROW BY ROW with the cause.

THE RESIDUE, all LOUD and all filed: an exit through an INDIRECT call or from
ANOTHER compilation unit dies with perl's own text (#1162's ruling, documented
in `docs/not-supported.md`); a `continue` block on a foreach or a bare block
declines the frame (#1161); a `sort` comparator is a boundary in perl and not
in PCL (#1164).  #1163 CLOSED by the narrowing.
subject: An UNLABELLED `last`/`next` inside a CALLED SUB does not reach the caller's loop -- perl exits it (with an "Exiting subroutine via last" warning); PCL either silently runs the loop to completion or dies "attempt to GO to nonexistent tag: :next".  The LABELLED spelling is correct.
